newsitem.title: GERMANY: German minister - Krupp-Thyssen deal possible today.
newsitem.headline: German minister - Krupp-Thyssen deal possible today.

text.p: German steel group Krupp and Thyssen could sign an initial memorandum of understanding to merge their steel companies later today, a state minister said on Wednesday.

Wolfgang Clement, economics minister of North Rhine-Westphalia state, also told reporters that the two companies could invest up to one billion marks in Krupp's steel works in Dortmund, countering fears it would be shut down.
Clement added that the investment would probably be made in a new hot galvanising unit -- to coat sheet steel for the car industry -- and in the existing cold-rolling mill.
The programme to merge the two steel companies would run to the year 2002.
The economics minister also said that Krupp would face the brunt of around 8,000 job cuts to be made when the two steel companies are merged.
Around 3,600 jobs at Krupp Hoesch Stahl AG would be cut from a workforce of some 5,700 at the Dortmund-based steel works.
Krupp and Thyssen have pledged to create around 1,300 jobs in Dortmund in other areas to limit the total number of jobs that would be lost in the city, he added.

Earlier, Ekkehard Schulz, head of Thyssen's steel company, Thyssen Stahl AG, said that of around 8,000 job cuts planned, 4,000 had been agreed previously in restructuring in areas where the two companies already co-operate.
The additional 4,000 job cuts were the only redundancies directly related to the merger with Krupp Hoesch Stahl AG.
Clement added that of the total job cuts planned, around 1,000 would be in administration.
The two companies would probably issue a hiring freeze and offer voluntary severance packages to accelerate workforce reductions, he said.
He added that more detailed issues such as the future of particular manufacturing sites or coke requirements had not been finalised yet.
The companies have said they would work out the details of the steel merger over the next four weeks.
